header.title: Peter Lynch's Playbook
header.subtitle: How an $18M fund became $14B in 13 years

hook_paragraph: Peter Lynch ran Fidelity Magellan from 1977 to 1990. Over those 13 years he averaged 29.2% annualized — beating the S&P 500 by ~13.4 percentage points per year. Magellan AUM grew from $18M to $14B, a 777x scale-up. Here is the playbook that did it, on one page.

primary_chart.title: Magellan vs. S&P 500 (1977-1990)
primary_chart.source: Wikipedia — Fidelity Magellan Fund / Quartr Insights

items.name: Buy What You Know
items.description: Lynch's wife Carolyn loved L'eggs at the supermarket. Lynch bought Hanes (the maker) — the stock returned 6x. The retail investor's edge is daily observation: malls, supermarkets, restaurants.

items.name: Do Your Homework
items.description: Read every annual report. "2-min pitch" — explain the company clearly. Pursue high earnings, low debt, long runway. Numbers must back the story. Lynch popularized PEG = P/E ÷ Growth %.

items.name: Six Stock Categories
items.description: Match expected return to the bucket. Slow Growers (2-4%), Stalwarts (10-12%), Fast Growers (20-25%+, Lynch's favorite), Cyclicals, Turnarounds, Asset Plays.

secondary_chart.title: Lynch's Field-Research Multibaggers
secondary_chart.source: One Up on Wall Street, Beating the Street

items: Track PEG < 1 in companies you actually use as a customer
Read 10-K filings quarterly — Lynch read ~700 / yr
Categorize before sizing — Fast Grower position ≠ Stalwart position
